# frostmoln_mysql_instance (Data Source)

Look up a MySQL instance by ID or name. Exactly one of `id` or `name` must be specified.

This is how a configuration reaches a database that Terraform did not create: an instance provisioned in the portal or with `fm` can today be referenced only by a hardcoded UUID or plumbed through `terraform_remote_state` — both of which tie the configuration to one deployment. Look it up by name instead and the reference survives re-provisioning elsewhere.

A name lookup that matches NOTHING fails the read, and so does one that matches MORE THAN ONE instance: the data source refuses to pick for you (the diagnostic names the colliding ids). A `postgresql` instance never satisfies this data source, by id or by name — use `frostmoln_postgres_instance`. There is no composed `endpoint` attribute: the platform serves the instance's address as `private_ip`/`public_ip` plus `port`, which is the wire shape every client composes from.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Resolve a MySQL instance that Terraform did not create
# (provisioned in the portal or with `fm`) by NAME — no hardcoded UUID.
data "frostmoln_mysql_instance" "orders" {
  name = "orders"
}

# The resolved instance feeds references elsewhere — e.g. an allow-list or an
# application server's connection string (no composed endpoint attribute
# exists on the wire: compose host and port).
locals {
  orders_address = coalesce(data.frostmoln_mysql_instance.orders.public_ip, data.frostmoln_mysql_instance.orders.private_ip)
}

# A lookup by id behaves identically for instances whose UUID is already known.
data "frostmoln_mysql_instance" "by_id" {
  id = data.frostmoln_mysql_instance.orders.id
}

# A name that matches nothing — or more than one MySQL instance — fails
# the read loudly rather than picking an instance for you.
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `id` (String) The unique identifier of the MySQL instance. Exactly one of id or name must be specified.
- `name` (String) The name of the MySQL instance. Exactly one of id or name must be specified.

### Read-Only

- `admin_username` (String) The admin username for the instance. The admin password is never served by the read surface.
- `backup_enabled` (Boolean) Whether backups are enabled.
- `backup_retention_days` (Number) How many days backups are retained, null when unset.
- `backup_schedule` (String) The backup schedule, null when backups are not enabled.
- `created_at` (String) The timestamp when the instance was created.
- `flavor_id` (String) The flavor ID/size of the instance.
- `ha_enabled` (Boolean) Whether high availability is enabled.
- `ha_status` (String) The high-availability status, null when HA is not enabled.
- `parameter_group_id` (String) The parameter group attached to the instance, null when the instance runs on server defaults.
- `port` (Number) The port the instance listens on.
- `private_ip` (String) The private IP address of the instance. Compose the connection address with `port` — the platform serves no composed endpoint attribute.
- `public_ip` (String) The public IP address of the instance, null when the instance is not publicly reachable.
- `security_group_id` (String) The platform-managed security group attached to the instance. The platform creates and owns it: rule writes on it are refused (read it with `frostmoln_security_group_rules`); import it only to understand it, never to manage it.
- `status` (String) The current status of the instance.
- `storage_gb` (Number) The storage size in gigabytes.
- `subnet_id` (String) The subnet ID where the instance is deployed.
- `tenant_id` (String) The tenant ID that owns this instance.
- `type` (String) The database type. Always `mysql` on this data source — the type is checked on every path, so the value is platform-verified, not a restatement of the configuration.
- `updated_at` (String) The timestamp when the instance was last updated, null when the platform has not recorded one.
- `version` (String) The MySQL version (the wire's typeVersion).
- `vpc_id` (String) The VPC ID where the instance is deployed.
